summary: EU-West cost spike: Nordic Bank reporting higher $/1M output tokens in weekly cost transparency report
description:
Customer (Nordic Bank) contacted Support after reviewing the weekly cost transparency export they receive from Redwood CS (internal pull from early Unit Economics views). They report an apparent "cost spike" isolated to eu-west: blended $/1M output tokens increased ~30–40% week-over-week for their primary chat workload.

They are requesting:
1) Confirmation whether Redwood changed pricing in eu-west (they suspect a regional multiplier)
2) Root cause for why eu-west appears materially more expensive than prior weeks
3) Whether the numbers are trustworthy (they are using this for internal monthly chargeback)

---
Customer report
- Time window: 2025-02-03 through 2025-02-10 (week-over-week comparison vs 2025-01-27 through 2025-02-03)
- Region: eu-west only
- Workload: chat/generation (majority streaming) + smaller embeddings volume
- What changed (per customer): no major traffic increase, no prompt changes, no model switch on their side

Impact
- Internal finance flagged this as a potential issue; customer asked for written explanation by EOW.
- Customer is enterprise and sensitive about EU residency; they are evaluating expanding volume but want cost predictability.

Environment / context
- This is not the customer-facing Console spend view (which is based on billable token pricing).
- The metric in question is Redwood’s internal "blended $/1M output tokens" from the Unit Economics pipeline used for internal reporting and (for this customer) an early transparency export.

---
Investigation notes (internal)
Owner: Caleb Johnson (Data Quality), with help from Nadia Rahman (Token metering) and Quentin Harris (Model metadata).

1) Confirmed spike exists in early Unit Economics views
- Query: hourly aggregates grouped by (region, customer, model, quantization_profile)
- Result: step-function increase in blended $/1M output tokens starting ~2025-02-04 01:00 UTC, isolated to eu-west and primarily the rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct traffic.

2) Checked whether this is a cost input (rate card) change
- Compared rate card version for eu-west between weeks.
- No rate card update applied in that window (no change in GPU hourly assumptions).

3) Checked whether this is a token denominator issue (undercount / missing dims)
- No evidence of missing output tokens for Nordic Bank in the affected hours.
- Completeness checks: passed for region + tier coverage; no "unknown_region" surge.
- Streaming vs non-streaming share stable week-over-week.

4) Identified primary driver: quantization profile shift in eu-west
- The eu-west serving pools for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct shifted from a quantized profile (q4/awq variant) to fp16 for a subset of capacity starting 2025-02-04.
- In the Unit Economics breakdown, cost per output token for fp16 was materially higher and became the dominant share of served tokens in eu-west.
- Cross-check: other regions did not show the same profile mix shift.

5) Secondary contributing signals
- Slight batching efficiency decrease (p50 concurrent decode batch size down) during peak CET hours, consistent with more heterogeneous sequence lengths that week.
- Cache hit rate signals (prefix/KV) were not the main driver; they were within normal week-to-week variance for this customer.

Root cause hypothesis (validated with Runtime on-call)
- A stability mitigation/rollback in eu-west disabled the quantized kernel/profile for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct due to an elevated error rate observed in that region’s fleet after a driver rollout.
- The scheduler/routing in eu-west preferred the "safe" fp16 profile until the driver issue was cleared.
- This increased GPU-hours per output token and therefore the blended $/1M output token metric.

Customer-facing vs internal metric clarification
- This did NOT change Nordic Bank’s contract token pricing (no pricing change).
- The transparency export they receive is an internal "cost" metric, and the increase reflects a real (temporary) increase in Redwood’s underlying cost to serve in eu-west for that workload.

---
Resolution / response sent to customer
- Confirmed: no pricing change in eu-west.
- Explained: their eu-west cost metric increased due to a temporary serving profile change (quantized -> fp16) applied for stability; this change was region-specific.
- Provided timeline: started 2025-02-04 01:00 UTC; mitigation in place through 2025-02-10; working on returning eu-west to quantized profile once validated.
- Set expectation: we will annotate the next transparency export with a note for that week; if they need a finance-safe summary, we can provide an "adjusted" view that separates (a) rate-card changes vs (b) serving-profile mix changes.

---
Follow-ups / action items
1) Runtime/SRE: confirm ETA to re-enable quantized profile in eu-west after driver validation and run a canary on Nordic Bank-like traffic mix.
2) Unit Economics team: add an alert for abrupt quantization_profile mix shifts by region for top enterprise customers (to catch future spikes before the weekly export).
3) CS Ops: add a short footnote template to the transparency export clarifying that "blended $/1M output tokens" can move due to fleet/profile mix, even without customer-side changes.

Internal notes / caveats
- This ticket uses early Unit Economics pipeline data; confidence is high for the directionality and the driver (profile mix) but we should continue to treat week-by-week comparisons as "operational" until Finance signoff gates are met (reconciliation report + methodology v1).
